title: Git Projects v2: See What Is Really Checked Out on Each Server
description: The Git projects page now finds the repositories on your servers and shows their real state, instead of relying only on the projects you registered by hand.
highlights: A new On the servers panel lists every repository found on each SSH target with its branch, commit, changed files and whether the remote has moved on, rescanned every 5 minutes or on demand.

Labels come from what the server observes: changed files, not on the default branch, update available or N behind, up to date, remote unreachable. The same repository at different commits on two servers is called out.
Hide repositories that are not your projects. Tracked projects no longer show a green Up to date before GitHub has been checked, and records whose folder is missing on their host are flagged.

title: Logs v2: Detailed Cloudflare Entries, System Events, Filters and Export
description: The Logs page now records what happens on its own, not only what you click, and its Cloudflare entries say which tunnel and what changed.
highlights: Cloudflare entries name the tunnel and the action: published, origin changed, moved from one tunnel to another, DNS repaired or removed, and failures say which tunnel.

System events are logged when status changes: containers that exit, restart, become unhealthy or disappear, Docker hosts going unreachable, Cloudflare tunnels going down or coming back, backup results and dashboard updates.
Filter by date range and actor, and download the filtered entries as CSV or JSON (exports follow privacy mode).

title: Cloudflare Tunnel Manager, Grouped Navigation, Fleet and Mobile Polish
description: A new Cloudflare page manages every tunnel and domain on your account with a traffic map, the sidebar is grouped with Settings as its own page, and Fleet, Logs, Processes and the phone layout were reworked.
highlights: Cloudflare page: lists all remotely-managed tunnels and zones, draws domain to tunnel to origin, flags missing or wrong DNS records, and publishes, edits, moves or removes hostnames. Needs CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID.
Sidebar groups (Infrastructure, Network, Develop, Automation, System) with a phone bottom bar; Settings is now a page and its theme buttons really switch the theme.
Fleet: search across all hosts, status and sort filters, list, cards and table views, and View all now shows every container (page sizes 15, 30 and All).
Logs paginate and Processes become cards on phones; tables no longer overflow, tap targets are at least 40px, text is at least 11px, and the light theme passes WCAG AA contrast.
Privacy mode now also masks IPs and domains inside log lines and process command lines; failed loads show a Retry instead of an empty page.

title: Real SSL Certificate Checks, Sentinel Bot Hardcode Cleanup
description: The SSL certificates panel now performs a real TLS handshake against each configured domain instead of showing six invented sample certificates, and the Telegram Sentinel bot no longer bakes this owner's specific hardware and IPs into its replies.
highlights: New SSL_DOMAINS env var: list the domains to track (host[:port][=Label]) and the panel checks their actual certificate expiry, cached and re-checked on SSL_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS (default 6h) rather than fabricating data.
An unreachable domain shows clearly as unreachable instead of a plausible-looking fake reading; demo mode keeps its own sample data.
Sentinel bot: hardware/IP/storage details in /help and the Gemini assistant context now come from live telemetry and config instead of hardcoded strings.

title: Perf: Delta-Only WebSocket Broadcast
description: The live dashboard feed now sends only the parts of the snapshot that actually changed since the previous 2-second tick instead of the entire snapshot every time, cutting payload size and serialization work on sections like SSL certificates and Git projects that rarely change.
highlights: Periodic WebSocket updates now carry only changed top-level snapshot sections; a newly connected browser still always gets the full snapshot first.
No visible behavior change — this is a transport-level optimization, the dashboard still updates every 2 seconds.

title: Perf: Docker Stats Streaming, Cheaper Thermal Read
description: Container CPU/memory monitoring now reads from one persistent stats stream per running container instead of polling every container's stats over a fresh Docker API call each 2-second tick, and CPU package temperature reads /sys/class/thermal directly instead of probing sensors on every poll.
highlights: Docker container monitoring: one open stats stream per running container (capped at 30) replaces a per-container stats() round-trip every tick; streams close automatically when a container stops or monitoring mode turns off.
CPU temperature: reads a cached /sys/class/thermal zone directly; falls back to the heavier sensor-probing library only on platforms without a usable zone, throttled to once per 30 seconds.

title: Fix: Host CPU% and Disk Performance Accuracy
description: Host CPU usage now reflects real utilization from /proc/stat instead of load average, disk performance resolves each mount to its actual block device instead of guessing from the mount path's own name, and a snapshot no longer hides that the primary host fell back to demo data just because a secondary host stayed connected.
highlights: Host CPU%: computed from a /proc/stat idle/total delta between polls, matching how load-average-independent monitoring tools measure utilization; falls back to the old load-average estimate only on platforms without /proc/stat.

Disk performance: mounts are matched to /proc/diskstats by their real major:minor device identity instead of a substring guess on the mount path ('media'/'cloud'/'music'); a mount that can't be resolved (e.g. LVM/device-mapper) now shows 'not available' instead of fabricated numbers.

Snapshot honesty: each Docker host's 'connected' status now reflects that tick's actual fetch result, and isDemoMode is keyed off the primary host specifically instead of any configured host being live.

title: Git Projects: Pull & Rebuild Over SSH
description: Tracked projects can now be pulled and rebuilt on a separate Docker host or LXC, not just the one Homelab Cockpit itself runs on — pick an SSH target in the edit dialog and the pull and rebuild run there instead.
highlights: Track a Git Project: new 'Runs on' selector lists your configured SSH targets (the same ones Terminal and Processes use) alongside the default 'this daemon' option.
With an SSH target picked, Local path becomes an absolute path on that remote host instead of a folder name under GIT_PROJECTS_ROOT.
Pull & rebuild's live log, migration-risk check, and auto-deploy all work the same way for a remote target as they do locally — same fixed git/docker sequence, just run over SSH.
Docs: CLAUDE.md and the user manual updated; the standing single-host warning in the tracking form now explains the SSH target option instead.

title: Git Projects: Single-Host Limitation Warning
description: The Track a Git Project form now states plainly that pull & rebuild only works for containers running on the same Docker daemon as Homelab Cockpit itself — picking a different configured host in the tab strip only filters the container list, it doesn't extend where the rebuild can run.
highlights: Track a Git Project: added a standing warning explaining that pull & rebuild always targets this daemon's own docker.sock, not a remote configured host.
Docs: CLAUDE.md and the user manual now document this scope explicitly alongside the existing primary-host-only services list.
.env.example: refreshed the DOCKER_HOSTS example entry to match the current host naming (yado-hosts).

title: Fix: Container Links Now Resolve to Their Own Docker Host
description: Container LAN/Tailscale links previously pointed at the primary Docker host's IP regardless of which configured host the container actually ran on. Fixed so each host resolves its own LAN and Tailscale address.
highlights: Container Fleet: containers on additional Docker hosts (e.g. whitearchive-hosts) now get LAN/Tailscale links pointing at that host's own IP, not the primary host's — fixes clicking a container's port badge opening the wrong service when both hosts happened to use the same port.
Docker hosts without a configured Tailscale IP (not yet joined the tailnet) no longer inherit the primary host's Tailscale address.
New env config: DOCKER_HOST_LAN_IP / DOCKER_HOST_TAILSCALE_IP for the primary host, and an extended DOCKER_HOSTS format (name=url|lanIp|tailscaleIp) for additional hosts.

title: Shortcut Group Management, Full Logs Inspector & English Localization
description: Streamlined shortcut management with group rename & deletion modal, removed manual drag/drop order and duplicate repo link, added full log inspector for system audit trails and container logs, and unified the entire dashboard interface into English.
highlights: Shortcut Groups Management: Easily rename custom groups or delete groups with options to keep or remove associated shortcuts.
Streamlined Shortcuts: Removed drag-and-drop manual ordering and duplicate repository link in favor of automatic group sorting and the dedicated Homelab Updater.
Full System & Container Logs: Added detailed inspector modal for system audit logs with copy-to-clipboard raw payloads, plus expanded container log tailing options (up to 1,000 lines or full output).
Unified English Localization: All user interface labels, alerts, update banner states, and tooltips are now cleanly synchronized in English.

title: Full Container Management, System Logs Page & UI Overhaul
description: UI overhaul (sticky sidebar, tidier header, interaction animations) plus new features: full container management (start/stop/restart, default card view, pinned filter, sort), a Logs page with a complete audit trail, pull & redeploy timestamps in Git Projects, shortcut grouping, and extra detail in the AI Agents Monitor.
highlights: The sidebar is now truly sticky to the viewport while scrolling, instead of scrolling along with the content.
Header tidied up: the Settings/Fullscreen/Refresh/Sign out buttons are merged into a single 'More' menu to reduce clutter.
Container Fleet: Card view by default, Pinned/All filter, and full start/stop/restart control per container.
New Logs page: a complete audit trail (auth, pin, container, git, backup, config, error) with category/level filters and search.
Git Projects shows the time and date of the last pull & redeploy.
Shortcuts (Bookmarks) can now be grouped into custom groups.
AI Agents Monitor shows turns today, last active time, and a transparency disclaimer that the 5-hour/weekly figures are local estimates, not official account limits.

title: Standalone Out-of-Process Redeployer & Seamless Service Reconnect
description: Adds a standalone execution script on the host (scripts/homelab-redeploy.sh & /root/homelab-redeploy.sh) and a watcher daemon for a redeploy process that survives container termination, plus smart auto-reconnect when the service briefly goes down.
highlights: Standalone Host Redeployer (scripts/homelab-redeploy.sh): A standalone script on the host (/root/homelab-redeploy.sh) that performs auto-stash, fetch, reset, auto-heal of the 'homelab-net' Docker network, and docker compose up -d --build --force-recreate without being cut off when the cockpit container restarts.

Watcher / Daemon Mode (--watch): A trigger-file monitoring daemon that can run on the host or as a systemd service (scripts/homelab-redeploy.service) to pick up redeploy commands from the web dashboard in real time.

Seamless Downtime & Auto-Reconnect: When the container is being recreated and the connection drops briefly ('service briefly down'), the dashboard UI shows a 'Service Restarting' transition status instead of a fatal error, polls /api/health periodically, and reloads automatically once the new container is up ('back up again').

title: Removed Beta UI & Instant Primary Node Customization
description: Removes the Beta UI routes and layout entirely to simplify the interface back to Classic Glassmorphism, and fixes the persistence and broadcast bug for the custom Primary Node name.
highlights: Cleaned up Beta UI: Removed the /beta layout, header, sidebar, and routes entirely so the dashboard stays focused on the stable main interface.
Instant Primary Node Name: Fixed the WebSocket broadcast and settings write so a custom Primary Node name applies instantly across all views.
Streamlined User Settings: Focused the settings modal on node name customization, color theme (Dark/Light), and owner account security.

title: User Settings Hub, Node Renaming & Git Project Failure Recovery
description: Adds a unified User Settings panel for theme and UI Style customization (Classic Glassmorphism vs Neo-Brutalism), Primary Node renaming, owner login password change, and a Repull & Redeploy recovery button when a Git project status is failed.
highlights: User Settings Hub: A comprehensive settings modal for choosing UI Style (Classic Glassmorphism vs Neo-Brutalism), Color Theme (Dark/Light), and display preferences.
Dynamic Primary Node Name: Change the Primary Node label (PVE / host) directly from the dashboard, stored on the server and broadcast in real time via WebSocket.
Password Management: Change the owner account / one-time login password with secure scrypt verification and new password confirmation.

Git Project Failure Recovery: Provides Repull & Redeploy (Force Sync) and Retry Check buttons when an upstream check fails or the status is failed, plus automatic cleanup of a leftover .git/index.lock file.

title: Full Feature Parity & Shortcuts System for Beta Brutalist UI
description: Completes the Beta Brutalist UI with every feature previously found only in the Legacy UI: Command Palette internal routing, bookmark shortcuts with brutalist card styling, a notification panel, collapsible sidebar, CPU thermal sensors, and a quick action deck.
highlights: Integrated Shortcuts & Bookmarks: Brings back Personal Web Shortcuts in HomePageBeta with high-contrast brutalist styling, an empty state action, and a card hover effect.
Command Palette Preservation: Ctrl+K navigation inside the Beta UI now automatically keeps the /beta/* routes so users are not thrown back to the Legacy UI.
Collapsible Beta Sidebar: Adds an expand/collapse toggle to BetaSidebar with localStorage persistence for a larger workspace.
Complete Vitals & Telemetry Parity: Adds CPU load %, RAM used/total, Package Temp / Thermal temperature sensors, and a Quick Action launchpad to the Beta Overview.

title: Force Pull & Auto-Stash Resilient Git Project Redeploy
description: Eliminates pull & redeploy failures caused by local change conflicts in repository files (e.g. docker-compose.yml), using a clean force pull via git fetch & reset --hard plus a data-protecting auto-stash.
highlights: Force Pull Pipeline: Replaces the standard git pull with git fetch + git reset --hard origin/<branch> to ensure containers always redeploy without the Aborting error.

Auto-Stash Data Protection: Local changes to tracked files are automatically saved to a git stash before the reset, while untracked files (.env, database directories, data volumes) stay safe and untouched.

title: Fix Window Auto-Scroll Lock during App Update
description: Fixes a bug where the browser window was forcibly pulled down while "Updating dashboard..." was running, so users can now scroll up freely and read the log without interruption.
highlights: Container-Scoped Auto-Scroll: Replaces the global scrollIntoView() call with scrollTo({ top: scrollHeight }) directly on the AppUpdateBanner terminal container.
Scroll Freedom: Prevents hijacking of the browser window scroll while the update log refreshes every second, letting users freely view the top of the modal and the dashboard.

title: Beta UI Brutalist Perfection & Dedicated Storage SMART Watchdog
description: Thorough Brutalist visual polish for the Beta UI, mobile phone responsiveness optimization, and splitting Storage & DAS Watchdog into a standalone section with SMART and real-time I/O telemetry.
highlights: Dedicated Storage & DAS Watchdog: Moves the storage panel out of a narrow column into a full standalone section in InfraPage, with LVM-thin allocation and container workload details.
Real-Time SMART & I/O Telemetry: Shows SMART status (PASSED/WARNING), live read/write throughput (MB/s), disk active time %, and response latency directly.
Enhanced Canary Watchdog: Live visualization of .mounted file detection status with a pulse indicator to prevent root filesystem overflow when the external enclosure disconnects.
Overview Real-time Storage Vital: Adds a Storage & DAS Watchdog summary block to the Core Vitals grid on the Beta HomePage.
Universal Brutalist Styling: Rounded-none corner reset, backdrop blur disabled, custom brutalist scrollbars, and snappy 0.08s animations across the whole Beta interface.
Mobile UX Refinement: Ergonomic horizontal navigation bar and tidy header actions without horizontal overflow on phone screens.

title: Beta UI Overview Feature Parity & Mobile Support
description: Brings the Beta UI main dashboard to feature parity with the Legacy version and adapts the layout for phone screens.
highlights: Feature Parity: Adds the App Update Banner and the Bookmarks Shortcuts panel to the Beta HomePage (Brutalist UI)
Mobile CSS Grid: Fixes column class styling for phone layouts (e.g. using grid-cols-1 vs grid-cols-2) so the Brutalist grid stays tidy and does not overlap on narrow screens

title: Smart Auto-Scroll Logs & Force Update Button
description: UX fixes for the live update terminal and a new force button for the App Updater, resolving complaints about the window scroll being locked automatically.
highlights: Smart Auto-Scroll: The log window during Git Project pull & redeploy and App Updater runs no longer forcibly locks the screen to the newest line if the user has deliberately scrolled up.
Force App Update: Adds a 'Pull & Redeploy' button in the Overview status bar (when the app is checked and already Up to date) so users can force the Dashboard update cycle to run again on their own.

title: Global Brutalist Beta UI Architecture & Layout Engine
description: Frontend architecture overhaul that adds a standalone Brutalist-style layout (Beta UI). All components and routes on the web now have two display modes globally, switchable instantly from a Header button.
highlights: Brutalist UI Mode: A pure constructivist interface design with thick borders, no blur, and a stark grid base
Global Layout Engine: Separates Legacy UI and Beta UI with a CSS environment blocker without duplicating page components
Header Seamless Toggle: A central button to switch between Classic UI and Beta UI with instant route navigation to `/beta/`
Documentation Update: Cleaned out old screenshots in the README, leaving the main dashboard interface overview

title: Real-Time Update Engine, Fleet Card Sorting & T3 Volume Wire
description: Self-updater engine upgrade with real-time background commit monitoring, robust auto-recovery rebase when local git diverges, flexible sorting in Fleet Card View, and T3 Code persistence volume integration.
highlights: Real-Time Updater: Automatic detection of GitHub commit updates in the background every 30-60 seconds without reloading the page
Auto-Fetch & Resilient Rebase: Automatic git fetch when checking for updates and smart recovery if the local branch diverges
Fleet Cards Sort Controls: Sort containers by Name, CPU, RAM, or Network with an ASC/DESC toggle in card mode
T3 Code Volume Integration: Mounts the T3 Code data volume read-only in docker-compose for seamless AI Agent telemetry

title: AI Agents Monitor, Glassmorphism UI & Fleet Cards View
description: Adds multi-tenant AI Agent usage monitoring (Claude Pro & Gemini) straight from T3 Code telemetry, a modern Glassmorphism interface with smooth transitions, a card display mode (Cards vs Table) for the container fleet, and updater stability fixes.
highlights: AI Agents Monitor: Track usage of 4 AI agents (Claude Pro, Gemini Default, Auth, Marmut) with a 5-hour sliding limit and a second-by-second cooldown countdown
Weekly History & Interaction Stream: A 7-day bar chart per agent and a real-time model execution log
Glassmorphism Visual Design: Modern transparent panels with backdrop blur, border glow, and fade-in-up animations
Fleet Cards vs Table View: Toggle between a grid card layout and a responsive table in Container Fleet
Self-Updater Stability: Monorepo npm workspaces automation and fixes for build execution in the production container

title: Automatic Update Feature, Drag & Drop Shortcuts & Header Cleanup
description: The dashboard can now be updated straight from Overview with one click, no manual pull & redeploy needed. Adds an automatic update announcement system from commits/announcements, shortcut reordering with drag & drop, fully clickable shortcut cards, and cleanup of hardware info in the header.
highlights: One-Click Update of homelab-dashboard from Overview without manual pull & redeploy
Automatic update announcement system with an update summary
Shortcut straight to the GitHub repository
Reorder shortcuts with Drag and Drop, then click Save
The whole shortcut box is clickable to open the link in a new tab
Cleanup of the PVE, Docker host, Tailnet, Containers, and CPU hardware info strip in the Header
